newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's TSUM store issues shares to reconstruct.
newsitem.headline: Russia's TSUM store issues shares to reconstruct.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest retailers, OAO Torgovy Dom TSUM, will launch a 30 million share issue on Tuesday at 2,000 roubles (37 U.S. cents) to pay towards a big modernisation programme, the lead manager of the issue said on Monday.
The shares will be on offer until December 31, 1996, Oleg Yachnik, president of lead manager OLMA told a news conference.
TSUM, located in the centre of Moscow near the Bolshoi Theatre, is one of the first major Russian companies to make a share issue to raise funds.

The $22 million reconstruction project, which aims to put a gloss on the store for the city of Moscow's 850th anniversary next September, will increase floor space by 60 percent from the current 9,300 square meters, TSUM general manager Alexader Voskoboinikov said.
If all the shares are sold the issue will raise about $12 million, and Voskoboinikov said the rest of the project cost would be covered from TSUM's cash flow and by bank loans.
TSUM shares rose to $0.360 on the Russian Trading System from $0.335 at Friday's close.
OLMA already has preliminary bids for up to 70 percent of the new issue, Yachnik said, and five to seven percent will be set aside for small investors.
French bank Societe Generale is agent for the issue.
TSUM, whose history goes back to 1885, had a profit before tax of 21.1 billion roubles in 1995 on sales of 53.5 billion.
TSUM is modernising its premises to capitalise on the spending power of Russia's emerging middle class, as Russia shows signs of pulling out of recession.
But the top end of the retail market is becoming increasingly competitive.
TSUM is located near Russia's biggest retailer GUM, which has a prime site on Red Square facing the Kremlin, and the Petrovsky Passazh luxury mall.
Nearby the city council is building the Manezhnaya Ploshchad shopping mall for the capital's 850th anniversary.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad issued shares in August to raise $35 million and plans to issue a further $50-60 million worth of shares in November or December.

The Moscow city government is TSUM's biggest shareholder with a 24.5 percent stake, Swiss private bank Pictet & Cie has 6.71 percent, OLMA-Bank has 5.03 percent and AOOT Russ-Invest, a Russian investment fund, has about 5.5 percent.
